newsitem.title: INDIA: Reliance profit-taking caps Bombay share rally.
newsitem.headline: Reliance profit-taking caps Bombay share rally.

text.p: Share prices at Bombay exchanges ended a shade higher on Tuesday, capping an early rally triggered by Reliance shares, traders said.
The stock ended 0.25 rupees higher at 308.0 as profit-taking erased early surge after the firm reported better-than-expected results, they said.
"This is a pleasant surprise," said Jal Irani, Reliance analyst at Jardine Fleming India Broking Ltd.
Reliance Industries, India's largest private sector firm said its net profit rose to 13.23 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) from 13.05 billion in the previous year.
Reliance shares had rocketed nearly 19 percent in the last one week despite expectations of lower profits.
"It is a good result, but there is some profit-taking coming about," said Manish Nathwani, a dealer at brokers Samir Doshi.
The results were sharply above the consensus estimate of 12.06 billion rupees, according to a Reuter poll.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange ended 3.86 points, or 0.10 percent, higher at 3.803.65, below the intra-day high of 3,839.54.
Indian shares would trade narrowly as new Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral looked set to win a trust vote in parliament to be held later on Tuesday, analysts said.
"I think the market will take a breather," said Partha Roy Chowdhury, assistant director, equity trading, at securities firm Peregrine Capital in Hong Kong.
Analysts said the focus would now shift to key earnings of companies for the 1996/97 financial year due in the coming months.
"At this point we're asking investors to wait. The market should ease, it has run up a little too much," said Sandeep Nanda, head of research at Natwest Markets.
"Poor results will start coming in next month," he said.
Leading Indian firms in sectors like cement and steel are expected to announce a fall in net for 1996/97 due to a slowdown in demand and weak global prices of commodities.
"We have seen a run-up in prices in the last few days," said an equities dealer at a foreign brokerage. "It looks like all positive news is being factored in the market."

Shares of India's largest aluminium maker National Aluminium Company Ltd (NALCO) ended 1.75 rupees, or 3.36 percent, lower at 50.25 at the Bombay exchange on Tuesday after the firm announced a fall in its net profit.
NALCO on Tuesday said its net profit during 1996/97 (April-March) dropped to 4.79 billion rupees, from 5.35 billion a year earlier.
